targets.authors: Comabella M, Fernandez M, Martin R, Rivera-Vallve S, Borras E, Chiva C, Julia E, Rovira A, Canto E, Alvarez-Cermeno JC, Villar LM, Tintoré M, Montalban X
targets.title: Cerebrospinal fluid chitinase 3-like 1 levels are associated with conversion to multiple sclerosis.
targets.evidence_quote: In a previous proteomic study conducted by our group in pooled CSF samples, levels of apoAI, apoAIV, vitronectin, plasminogen, sema7A, and CNDP1 were found to be significantly different between CIS patients who converted to CDMS and patients who remained with CIS [ 5 ]. ApoAI was upregulated in CIS patients who converted to CDMS in all six CSF pools; apoAIV, vitronectin, and plasminogen were upregulated in four out of six pools. In contrast, sema7A and CNDP1 were downregulated in four out of six pools [ 5 ]. In the present study, we aimed to validate these proteins as biomarkers associated with the conversion to CDMS in individual CSF samples from CIS patients. Validation was performed in two stages, with a first replication study in CIS cohorts that had a partial overlap with the original pooled CIS cohort used for biomarker discovery (36% for cohort 1, 28% for cohort 2), and a second replication study conducted in CIS cohorts that were totally independent from the pooled CIS cohort.
targets.outcome_quote: Only apoAI, a specific inhibitor of proinflammatory cytokines secreted by activated T-cells [ 17 ], was found to be significantly increased in CSF from MS converters, but failed later validation in a totally independent cohort of CIS patients. Protein determinations in serum samples resulted in similar negative results. These proteins should therefore be considered as false positives found in the initial discovery proteomic approach [ 5 ]. Results from the present study validate two proteins, sema7A and CNDP1, as biomarkers associated with conversion to CDMS in CIS patients.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Two biomarkers validated; the remaining four original candidates were explicitly treated as false positives. The confirmation sentence concerns two proteins, not an overall verdict on all six.

reasoning: Identity and authors verified against Europe PMC. New and partly overlapping cohorts retest the published biomarker findings; the wholly independent validation cohorts distinguish this from reanalysis of original data.
